clue.text: Certain varieties of grass will reportedly cause bewilderment

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the verb

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: bamboos are tall grasses, and 'will' contracts to 'll after them

explanation.surface: A gardener warns that some ornamental grasses will baffle anyone trying to identify them.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'bamboos'll' (bamboos will) runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bamboozle someone is to trick or confuse them, leaving them in a state of puzzlement.

clue.text: Spanish city banishes a character in popular tale

indicators.note: to banish is to send away, so one letter is expelled from the city name

blocks.note: the Basque city in northern Spain
taken as written; this is the letter sent away

explanation.surface: A Spanish city expels some figure from a well-loved story.
explanation.walkthrough: BILBAO without its A leaves BILBO, as in Bilbo Baggins.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilbo Baggins is the hobbit hero of Tolkien's much-read novel The Hobbit.

clue.text: Gruesome sailor runs into club

indicators.note: going into something puts these letters inside the other word

blocks.note: a mace is a heavy spiked club
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: a seaman charges into a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre describes something grim and horrifying, concerned with death, which is what gruesome means.

clue.text: Old relative losing large amount of weight

indicators.note: losing something means it is dropped, so a letter disappears from the relative

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
L for large, as on clothing labels; the letter removed

explanation.surface: An elderly family member has slimmed down considerably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large amount of weight' reads as one phrase about dieting, but 'large' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a unit in the imperial system of measuring weight, one sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: Intense, mad look regularly adopted by Olympian

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
something adopted is taken in, so these letters go inside the god's name

blocks.note: chief of the gods on Mount Olympus

explanation.surface: An Olympic athlete wears a fierce, crazed expression before competing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' suggests a modern athlete; here it is the god of Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Zealous means fervent and passionate, showing strong commitment, as an intense person does.

clue.text: Former favourite welcoming study about setter's stratagem

definitions.note: noun sense of the answer: a means to an end

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so the favourite wraps around what follows
about means around, so the study surrounds the setter

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
a teacher's pet is a favourite
a den is a private study
the setter refers to themself as I; 'setter's' is 'setter is'

explanation.surface: An ex-favourite pupil adopts a cunning study plan devised by the puzzle-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: An expedient is a convenient means to achieve an end, a practical device or ruse.

clue.text: Fatuous paper written by attorney

blocks.note: a District Attorney in the US

explanation.surface: A lawyer has penned a silly document.
explanation.walkthrough: The paper comes second, after the attorney who wrote it.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft is the British informal word for silly or foolish, a close synonym of fatuous.

clue.text: Bare flesh is bound by quack with honorary title

indicators.note: something bound by another thing is wrapped inside it

blocks.note: a quack is a doctor, abbreviated DR
Officer of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: A dodgy doctor with a royal honour has the patient strip off.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' in the clue is a letter-source, not a verb; OBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To disrobe is to take off one's clothes, exposing the skin of the body.

clue.text: French POW sang about tapioca pudding

indicators.note: about can mean all around, in disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A French prisoner of war sings about the dessert served in the camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Tapioca pudding got its schoolchild nickname from the jelly-coated pearls resembling frog eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: British school slang compares the lumpy dessert to the clumps of eggs laid by frogs.

clue.text: Area behind factory occupied by church organ

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the area follows the rest
a place occupied by something holds it inside

explanation.surface: Behind the works is a plot taken over by a church, which installs its organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church organ' suggests a musical instrument; organ alone is the definition, the body's kind.
explanation.definitionFit: The placenta is a temporary body part in the womb that nourishes the developing foetus.

clue.text: Sucker turned to Russia's foremost spiritual adviser

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards
foremost means at the front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: a sap is a gullible person

explanation.surface: A gullible dupe looks to a Rasputin-like figure for spiritual guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a minister in charge of a congregation, giving religious guidance to its members.

clue.text: Serious lesion checked by doctor

indicators.note: a thing checked is held in or restrained, so the doctor sits inside

blocks.note: Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A worrying skin lesion is examined by a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: Sombre means grave or solemn in mood, which is the sense of serious here.

clue.text: Soldier on manoeuvres not comprehending international language

indicators.note: not comprehending means not including, so one letter is left out
troops on manoeuvres are moved about, so the letters are redeployed

blocks.note: I for international; the letter removed

explanation.surface: A soldier on exercises abroad can't understand the global tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier on' is both the fodder and part of a military surface; 'on manoeuvres' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse is the medieval Scandinavian tongue of the Vikings, ancestor of Icelandic.

clue.text: Posts sentimental thoughts on vacation

indicators.note: a word on vacation is emptied of its contents, leaving just its outer shell

explanation.surface: Someone on holiday shares mushy reflections online.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweet is to publish a short message on social media, which is what posting means.

clue.text: Unhappy with one's surroundings? Leave!

indicators.note: surroundings are what lies around the edge, so only the outer letters are used

blocks.note: W is an abbreviation for with
an old-fashioned command to go away

explanation.surface: If you dislike where you are, the advice is simply to go.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and exclamation turn the clue into a piece of blunt advice; 'one's' is just the word one with its surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Woebegone describes someone looking sad and miserable, full of sorrow.

clue.text: Tortured poet asks about love, in a way

indicators.note: something tortured is twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: love is nil in tennis, the shape of O

explanation.surface: An anguished poet questions love, after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'so to speak' flags a figurative expression, meaning roughly or in a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Emaciated, wild elk eats leaves, primarily

indicators.note: wild means uncontrolled, so these letters run loose into a new order
primarily means first of all, so only the initial letter counts

explanation.surface: A starving wild elk is reduced to eating leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Skeletal describes someone so thin that the bones show, extremely underweight.

clue.text: Communist circles reasonably satisfied

indicators.note: to circle something is to go around it, so the first word encloses the second

blocks.note: red is the colour of communism

explanation.surface: Party members in Marxist circles are fairly content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Communist circles' reads as a noun phrase; 'circles' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Requited love is returned and so fulfilled; a desire that is requited has been gratified.

clue.text: One taking over role of penny-pinching money lender

indicators.note: pinching means gripping, so the lender holds the coin inside

blocks.note: a usurer lends at extortionate interest

explanation.surface: A miserly loan shark muscles in on another's job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny-pinching' looks like one word meaning stingy; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurper seizes a throne or position without having the right to it.

clue.text: Clapped-out part from cherry-red Dodge is recycled

indicators.note: a part from something is a piece of it, so the letters lie inside the phrase
recycled suggests going back round the loop, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the letters found running across these words, read in clue order

explanation.surface: A worn-out bit from a red Dodge car goes for scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Doddery means shaky and feeble, especially from age, like an old car that is falling apart.

clue.text: Vehicles covered by extra insurance

indicators.note: covered by means concealed beneath, so the answer is tucked inside the words

explanation.surface: Some vehicles need extra insurance cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway carriages pulled by an engine are a form of transport for passengers and goods.

clue.text: River crossing in captivating German cathedral city

indicators.note: a river crossing a place runs through it, so the river splits around what follows
captivating literally means taking captive, so the small word holds the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A river runs through a charming German cathedral town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' suggests the city is in Germany; it is only a letter, and the city is in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Avignon in Provence has a cathedral beside the Palace of the Popes, which was the papal seat in the 14th century.

clue.text: Agent left in American vice squad finally revolted

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the next word
finally points to the end of each word, so last letters are kept

blocks.note: a rep is a sales agent
the last letters of both words

explanation.surface: An undercover operative joins a US vice squad, which finally rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolted here means disgusted, not rose up, though the police surface leans the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: To be repulsed is to feel strong disgust or aversion, the sense of revolted here.

clue.text: Minor offence

blocks.note: second meaning: an insult or snub

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a petty crime; the two words are separate meanings, the second a social affront rather than a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for something small and a noun for a discourteous snub.

clue.text: Prop essentially practises his sport in street

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the central letter is taken
in puts the preceding letters inside the street abbreviation

blocks.note: Rugby Union, the game a prop forward plays

explanation.surface: A rugby prop trains for his game out in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: A prop is a front-row forward in rugby, hence 'his sport'; but as definition prop means a support.
explanation.definitionFit: A strut is a rigid bar that braces a structure, a support exactly as a prop is.

clue.text: Catches extremely hideous constricting snake

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the two ends of the word
constricting means squeezing round, so the outer letters wrap the reptile

blocks.note: the small venomous snake of Cleopatra fame

explanation.surface: Someone captures a horribly ugly serpent that is squeezing its prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constricting' fits a snake, but it is the snake that gets squeezed here.
explanation.definitionFit: A hasp is a hinged metal fastening for a door or lid, a type of latch or clasp.

clue.text: Fall from highest place and ultimately survive

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so just the last letter is wanted

blocks.note: Pl. is the street-name abbreviation for place

explanation.surface: A champion falls from the top spot but hangs on in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall from highest place' reads as one phrase meaning the answer; only 'Fall' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple is to overbalance and tumble down, as a tower or a ruler might.

clue.text: Drunk is serene in other-worldly atmosphere

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy person feels calm in a dreamy, unreal setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Eeriness is a strange, uncanny feeling, as if something supernatural were present.

clue.text: Heckle old-time entertainer heartlessly

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle is removed, leaving just the edges

blocks.note: a court jester entertained medieval monarchs

explanation.surface: Cruelly barracking a music-hall comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle two letters of the six-letter word are its heart, and both go.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer is to shout mocking insults, which is what a heckler does to a performer.

clue.text: Prominent economist defending very accommodating model's principles

indicators.note: defending means shielding on all sides, so the economist surrounds the rest
accommodating means giving room to, so the small word holds the model

blocks.note: John Maynard Keynes, the British economist

explanation.surface: A leading economist defends the core ideas of an obliging model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' suggests a theory or a fashion model; it is the Model T, Ford's early car.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystone is the central stone of an arch, so figuratively the central tenet on which a system rests.
